summary.summary: Robert Kovil called to schedule a roofer to inspect and repair an issue on a rental home owned by his mother-in-law, Marilyn Warwick, after a large rainstorm (around November) led to drywall caving in the garage. An insurance company/adjuster inspected and indicated the problem was at a “dead valley” where the tile roof sections come together and needs to be fixed. The representative collected the property address (3553 N Ramada, Mesa, AZ 85215), confirmed it is a single-story tile roof with no HOA, not in a gated community, and no solar, and gathered contact details for both Robert and the legal owner. The rep explained what to expect during the 1–2 hour inspection appointment and scheduled the visit for Friday from 1–3 PM, which works for Robert (preferred after 10 AM).
key_points: Customer reported drywall caving in the garage after a big rainstorm (November) and said an insurance inspection identified an issue at a roof “dead valley” that needs repair.
Property details: tile roof, single-story home, no HOA, not gated, and no solar; address provided as 3553 N Ramada, Mesa, AZ 85215.
Appointment was scheduled for Friday between 1–3 PM; customer preferred anything after 10 and noted otherwise he doesn’t get home until about 5.
action_items: Complete on-site roof inspection and assess/diagnose the reported dead valley issue and any related leak/damage.
Collect the legal owner’s email address (Marilyn Warwick) at the appointment if needed for records/communication.
next_steps: Technician arrives Friday 1–3 PM, speaks with Robert, performs roof inspection, takes photos, and reviews findings/options with him.
Add/confirm Marilyn Warwick (legal owner) on the account and obtain her email during/after the visit.
